body.statement: Uniformly over compact subsets of \(\mathfrak R_{\varepsilon}\), under independent multinomial sampling and \(n/n_m\to\lambda\in(0,\infty)\) when margins are estimated, the deterministic selector \(\widehat\chi_n\) chooses an incident first-order-compatible rigid chart and \(\widehat\gamma_n=1\) with probability tending to one. On these certified separated rigid charts, \(\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}\), \(\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)\Rightarrow N(0,V_{\tau})\), and \(\widehat V_n\xrightarrow{P}V_{\tau}\). Because \(\lambda_{\min}(V_{\tau})\ge\varepsilon\), scalar contrasts and the elliptical branch of \(W_n\) have asymptotic coverage \(1-\alpha\). If no chart is certified, the total procedure returns \(\widehat\chi_n=\bot\), \(\widehat\tau_n=(0,0)\), \(\widehat V_n=I_2\), and \(W_n=[0,1]^2\), with no covariance-consistency or Wald-coverage assertion for that fallback branch.
body.justification: The chart rule, covariance formula, and nonsingularity margin make regular-stratum Wald inference operational and falsifiable.
body.gap: The anchor and earlier response-type estimators establish regular-case normality only for their inverse formulas, not for deterministically selected rational and simple algebraic rigid charts.
body.consumer: Separated empirical tables obtain reproducible standard errors and Wald regions on every first-order-compatible atlas chart.

obligation.what_is_open: Unconditional selector correctness for the claimed atlas on every separated rigid stratum.
obligation.obstruction: The delta-method calculation closes conditional on local atlas exhaustiveness, but an omitted mixed-support chart could invalidate the certification and incompatibility-distance step.
obligation.attempted: The multinomial covariance, chart-distance rate, common-Jacobian Taylor expansion, sandwich consistency, and fallback behavior were derived conditionally.
obligation.partial_result:
Conditional on local exhaustiveness of the certified atlas, the separated-stratum calculation is standard and explicit.  Independent multinomial sampling gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}.
\]
For every incident chart, the distance inequality
\(d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)\le\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) and \(t_n=n^{-1/4}\) make the distance test pass, while continuity and \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\) make the slack test pass.  The distance separation excludes incompatible charts.  Common values and Jacobians on incident charts, followed by a Taylor expansion, yield
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_{\chi}(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1),
\]
and hence covariance \(V_{\tau}\); positive definiteness and plug-in continuity give the Wald conclusion.  What is not yet available is the global compiler theorem that certifies the incident set and excludes an omitted mixed-support chart.
